title: Tech adoption friction heuristics — mini deck (draft)
content:
Purpose: quick, repeatable mini-deck for SEs to use when diagnosing adoption friction with platform/infra/engineer buyers. Not a full battlecard — this is a 6–8 slide, scenario-driven heuristic map plus play snippets.

Slide 1 — One line pitch (30s):
  • Why customers stall: adoption stalls almost always come from 1) cost surprises, 2) latency or tail-latency hits, 3) integration I/O complexity, or 4) uncertain model quality regressions.
  • Our job: identify which of the 4 is dominant, run a short probe, propose 1 low-friction pilot that proves value while containing risk.

Speaker note: say this in a 30s intro when handed to an engineer or platform architect. Keep it concrete — no product fluff.

Slide 2 — Rapid diagnosis checklist (2m):
  • Cost: token burn profiles? peak vs avg qps? Any unexpected embedding/async workloads?
  • Latency: P50/P95/P99 for generation and embed routes. Is tail driven by long-context requests?
  • Integration: are requests synchronous from UI? batching? do they use prefix caching?
  • Quality: have they compared a small evaluation set vs current model baseline?

Probe script (30s): ask engineer for three datapoints: current p95, token cost per response (approx), and whether they have a 10–20 prompt test set. If they can’t produce these, offer to run a 1-hour smoke-run on Redwood sandbox.

Slide 3 — Fast pilot patterns (2–4m):
  • Pilot A — Latency-first: pin a lightweight model variant (quantized), enable autoscale burst, set routing policy to region-local. Success criteria: p95 <= target and <2x cost baseline. Run 3-day traffic replay.
  • Pilot B — Cost-first: enable prefix cache + batching; route non-critical calls to a lower-cost variant; measure per-1000-token spend. Success: 30% unit cost reduction with <=10% quality delta on eval set.
  • Pilot C — Integration-lite: use async embed flow + background reranker to remove sync hammer. Success: UI TTFB improved by 40% and perceived latency drop by customer metrics.

Slide 4 — Objection snippets for common friction points (copy-paste):
  • "We can’t risk regressions." — "Agree; we propose a canary on 5% traffic with the same prompt set and automatic rollback if score drops >2 pts. We keep raw inputs private and only send masked traces for evaluation."
  • "Costs balloon with spikes." — "We’ll set a burst cap and route overflow to a cheaper fallback policy. Also propose a weekly batch run to profiled long-run unit economics."
  • "We need VPC/on-prem." — "We have Redwood Private; for pilots we can do a VPC-connected sandbox or a small dedicated pool with restricted network egress."

Slide 5 — Demo flow (2m demo script for SEs):
  1) Start with customer app: show 1 slow request and 1 failed high-cost example.
  2) Switch to Redwood Console — show per-route token and latency breakdown (token waterfall).
  3) Toggle a routing policy to a quantized variant and enable prefix caching (live change).
  4) Replay same request and show metrics delta.

Speaker tips: have a prepared noiseless replay dataset (5 requests). Keep the demo environment small so cold starts are predictable.

Slide 6 — Fallback economics quick table (for conversation):
  • Variant A (high perf): 1.0x baseline cost, p95 = 180ms
  • Variant B (quantized): 0.55x cost, p95 = 230ms (+28% latency)
  • Variant C (batch-cached): 0.35x cost, p95 best-effort async
  Use-case callouts: customer-facing chat = prefer A; batch summarization = prefer C; internal tools where latency can be relaxed = B or C.

Slide 7 — Pilot checklist (copyable):
  • Owner: SE + Eng contact assigned
  • Evaluation set: 20–50 prompts labeled with priority metrics (accuracy/ROUGE/semantic sim)
  • Timebox: 7–14 days
  • Success thresholds: define p95 and cost delta and quality delta in writing
  • Rollback plan: immediate traffic removal + alert to ops channel
  • Data handling: verify PII filter & KMS keys for logs

Slide 8 — Next steps and open questions (notes to self):
  • Quick asks: get their p95 and cost per 1k tokens before next call.
  • Internal ask: check whether the customer org has whitelist for private endpoints (PRIV-req).
  • Risk: if they use long-context streaming heavily, prioritize KV cache tuning — needs correlation with our runtime team.
  • TODO: create a short replay harness in repo quick-demos and attach a README with steps for SEs (linked PR noted above).

Appendix — Short scripts and artifacts:
  • 30s customer handoff script: "We’ll run a 7-day pilot, constrained to a 5% traffic canary, measure p95 and unit-cost, and share daily dashboards. If we miss threshold we pause and iterate. Does that sound reasonable?"
  • Jira templates: pilot-ticket template (JIRA-8472) includes fields: dataset_link, eval_metrics, rollback_contact, duration_days.
  • Confluence: internal playbook link for follow-up runbooks.

Loose notes / rough thoughts (keep in this doc):
  • Might add a small slide with real numbers from two recent pilots (anonymized) to increase credibility. Marco to pull redacted metrics.
  • Consider a one-click sandbox that seeds 20 prompts + metrics collection to reduce friction for SEs. Engineering feasibility: low-priority but high impact.
  • Format preference: split this into 1-slide cheat-sheet and a 6-slide mini-deck for customer-facing riff.

Unresolved questions to resolve before next review:
  • Who is the canonical owner for VPC sandbox requests? (ops or private-deployments?)
  • Which replay harness should we endorse (quick-demos PR referenced)? Need tag and README.
  • Should we publish a short internal leaderboard of model variants and their cost/p95 typical ranges? (good for SEs)

End of draft — intentionally terse. Use this as a live doc for rapid SE training and to spin into a 6-card Slack training thread.
